title: The Static Promise
goal: A function with no inputs returns a &str. What must it promise — and what can keep that promise?
hints: No inputs means no input lifetimes to borrow from. Only one lifetime remains.
A literal lives in the binary forever. A String built inside the function dies at the brace — no annotation can save it.
explanation: With no borrowed inputs, elision has nothing to work with (E0106): the only lifetime a returned reference can honestly claim is 'static. And only truly immortal data qualifies — string literals are compiled into the binary, so "fearless concurrency" is &'static str for free. The String::from(...).as_str() variant borrows a temporary that dies at the semicolon (E0716/E0515), 'static annotation or not. The promise must match the data.
